title: Maya lowland wet interval (c. 440-660 CE)
summary: A precisely dated stalagmite from Yok Balum Cave in southern Belize records unusually high rainfall in the Maya lowlands from about 440 to 660 CE. The authors link this wet phase to population growth and a surge in Maya political centres; a drying trend followed from 660 to 1000 CE.

uncertainty.note: Range as stated in the Science abstract; a Penn State release gives AD 450-660.

where.modern_name: Southern Belize (Yok Balum Cave, near Uxbenka, Toledo District)

importance.justification: A dated rainfall record links a wet phase to Maya population growth and the spread of political centres.

sources.title: Development and disintegration of Maya political systems in response to climate change (Science 338:788-791)
sources.publisher: Northern Arizona University (research record of Kennett et al., Science)

reviewer_note: The pin is the cave region (cave about three miles from Uxbenka per Penn State), not a precise site. A single cave record; regional extent of the wet phase is the authors’ inference.
